hints: Focus on the carbon on the far right of each ring (C1, the anomeric carbon). Compare whether its OH is above or below the ring in A versus B, C and D.
Remember alpha means the C1 OH is below the ring (trans to the CH2OH), and glucose means the OH on C4 is also below the ring, unlike galactose where it is above.
walkthrough:
**Find the anomeric carbon C1**

Look at the carbon on the right side of the ring. This is C1. Its OH position tells you alpha or beta.

In alpha-glucose the $CH_2OH$ is up and the C1 $OH$ is down. In beta-glucose the C1 $OH$ is up.

**Separate alpha from beta**

Diagram A has the C1 $OH$ above the ring. That is beta, so A cannot be alpha-glucose.

Diagrams B, C and D all have C1 H above and C1 $OH$ below the ring. They are all alpha forms, so we need one more test.

**Check C4 to identify glucose**

Glucose and galactose are both $C_6H_{12}O_6$ but differ at C4 on the left side of the ring. D-glucose has the C4 $OH$ below the ring. D-galactose has the C4 $OH$ above the ring.

Only diagram B has the correct alpha C1 $OH$ down plus the glucose pattern at C2, C3 and C4. So B is alpha-glucose.

options.A: Shows a beta form because the C1 OH is above the ring, not below, so it cannot be alpha-glucose.
options.B: Shows C1 OH below the ring for alpha, with the C2, C3 and C4 OH pattern of glucose, including C4 OH below the ring.
options.C: Has alpha C1 OH below, but the C4 OH is above the ring, which is the galactose pattern, not glucose.
options.D: Has alpha C1 OH below, but the OH pattern at C2 is reversed to above the ring, which is not glucose.
